summary.en: A ladder selects the first true branch.
summary.bn: উপর থেকে শর্ত পরীক্ষা করে প্রথম মিলের কাজ চালাও এবং grading boundary ঠিক রাখো।

notes: else if is an else whose controlled statement is another if; it is not a separate C keyword. The structure works across C89 to C23. These examples use C17 and explicitly braced branches.

examples.title: Select a high grade
examples.explanationHtml: Seventy-seven fails the eighty threshold and passes seventy-five. The first matching branch prints A. It needs no explicit upper limit because reaching it already means the first test failed.

examples.title: Classify a signed difference
examples.explanationHtml: Zero fails both strict sign comparisons, so the final else handles it. These three categories cover every permitted integer. The output illustrates a final case whose meaning follows directly from the earlier failures.

examples.title: Use ascending size limits
examples.explanationHtml: Twenty-five exceeds the small-room limit but fits the medium-room limit. The ascending upper bounds must be ordered from smallest to largest. Reversing them would hide the small category inside the broader first condition.

practice.title: Three sign labels
practice.statementHtml: Read n -100 to 100. After the prompt Input: , print Negative, Positive or Zero and newline.
hints: Use strict comparisons before the zero fallback.

practice.title: Room capacity band
practice.statementHtml: Read n 0 to 100. After the prompt Input: , print Small up to 20, Medium from 21 to 40, otherwise Large; end the line.

practice.title: A simple grade report
practice.statementHtml: Read mark 0 to 100. After the prompt Input: , print A+ from 80, A from 75 to 79, Pass from 40 to 74, otherwise F; end with newline.

practice.title: Full classroom grade scale
practice.statementHtml: Read mark 0 to 100. After the prompt Input: , print the letter grade from the lesson table, then newline.
hints: Each earlier failure supplies the next upper bound.

quiz.prompt: How many matching branches does a ladder run?
quiz.explanation: The rest of the chain is skipped after a match.

quiz.prompt: For descending lower-bound grade tests, which threshold belongs first?
quiz.explanation: A broad low threshold would hide higher categories.

quiz.prompt: What is already known when the mark >= 75 branch follows a failed mark >= 80 test?
quiz.explanation: The earlier false condition supplies the upper limit.

quiz.prompt: Which keyword token is else-if in C?
options: It is two keywords, else and if
quiz.explanation: The else controls another if statement.

quiz.prompt: What should happen before grading an input mark?
options: Check that it belongs to the valid range
quiz.explanation: An impossible mark should not receive a normal grade.

quiz.prompt: How should ascending upper limits be ordered?
quiz.explanation: A larger first upper limit would capture smaller bands.

quiz.prompt: Which values best reveal a grade boundary error?
quiz.explanation: Neighbors show which side owns equality.

quiz.prompt: Seventy-five reaches which first matching grade?
quiz.explanation: The eighty test fails; seventy-five succeeds.

quiz.prompt: A zero value reaches which sign branch?
A high score stops at the first match. Which label prints?
quiz.explanation: The first true branch prevents the later branch from running.

examQuestions.question: How many matching branches does a ladder run?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Only the first. The rest of the chain is skipped after a match.

examQuestions.question: For descending lower-bound grade tests, which threshold belongs first?
examQuestions.answerHtml: The highest threshold. A broad low threshold would hide higher categories.

A

The eighty test fails; seventy-five succeeds.

examQuestions.question: Read mark 0 to 100. After Input: print the letter grade from the lesson table, then newline.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
#include <stdio.h>

int main(void)
{
    int mark;
    printf("Input: ");
    if (scanf("%d", &mark) != 1 || mark < 0 || mark > 100) {
        return 1;
    }
    if (mark >= 80) {
        puts("A+");
    } else if (mark >= 75) {
        puts("A");
    } else if (mark >= 70) {
        puts("A-");
    } else if (mark >= 65) {
        puts("B+");
    } else if (mark >= 60) {
        puts("B");
    } else if (mark >= 55) {
        puts("B-");
    } else if (mark >= 50) {
        puts("C+");
    } else if (mark >= 45) {
        puts("C");
    } else if (mark >= 40) {
        puts("D");
    } else {
        puts("F");
    }
    return 0;
}

Each earlier failure supplies the next upper bound.
